content: 1. Rilpivirine and Dofetilide: Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of dofetilide by prolonging the QTc interval. This combination should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. If co-administration is necessary, close monitoring is required. 2. Rilpivirine and Dolasetron: Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of dolasetron by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely when these drugs are co-administered. 3. Rilpivirine and Donepezil: Both rilpivirine and donepezil increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 4. Rilpivirine and Doxepin: Both rilpivirine and doxepin increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely when these drugs are used together. 5. Rilpivirine and Dronedarone: Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of dronedarone by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 6. Rilpivirine and Droperidol: Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of droperidol by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely when these drugs are co-administered. 7. Rilpivirine and Efavirenz: Efavirenz decreases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Additionally, both drugs increase the QTc interval, and co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 8. Rilpivirine and Eliglustat: Both rilpivirine and eliglustat increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 9. Rilpivirine and Elivaldogene Autotemcel: This combination may decrease the effects of one or both drugs. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Patients should not take antiretroviral medications for at least one month before initiating stem cell mobilization therapy and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 10. Rilpivirine and Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF: This combination is contraindicated. Elvitegravir-based regimens are complete HIV treatments and should not be co-administered with other antiretrovirals. 11. Rilpivirine and Encorafenib: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 12. Rilpivirine and Entrectinib: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 13. Rilpivirine and Eribulin: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 14. Rilpivirine and Erythromycin (Base, Ethylsuccinate, Lactobionate, Stearate): Erythromycin increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, and rilpivirine increases erythromycin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 15. Rilpivirine and Escitalopram: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 16. Rilpivirine and Eslicarbazepine Acetate: Eslicarbazepine decreases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Rilpivirine should not be co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inducers due to the risk of virologic failure and resistance. 17. Rilpivirine and Esomeprazole: Esomeprazole decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This combination is contraindicated. Concurrent use may lead to treatment failure and resistance. 18. Rilpivirine and Etravirine: Etravirine decreases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Rilpivirine should not be used with other NNRTIs. 19. Rilpivirine and Famotidine: Famotidine decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. Administer famotidine at least 12 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. Monitor closely for potential treatment failure. 20. Rilpivirine and Fexinidazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Avoid combining fexinidazole with drugs that block potassium channels or prolong the QT interval. 21. Rilpivirine and Fingolimod: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 22. Rilpivirine and Flecainide: Rilpivirine increases flecainide toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 23. Rilpivirine and Fluconazole: Fluconazole increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. No dose adjustment is required, but monitor closely for QTc prolongation and fungal infections. 24. Rilpivirine and Fluoxetine: Rilpivirine increases fluoxetine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 25. Rilpivirine and Foscarnet: Rilpivirine increases foscarnet toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 26. Rilpivirine and Fosphenytoin: Fosphenytoin decreases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 27. Rilpivirine and Fostemsavir: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 28. Rilpivirine and Gemifloxacin: Rilpivirine increases gemifloxacin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 29. Rilpivirine and Gepirone: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely during co-administration. 30. Rilpivirine and Gilteritinib: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 31. Rilpivirine and Givinostat: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Obtain ECGs during initiation and as clinically indicated. 32. Rilpivirine and Granisetron: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 33. Rilpivirine and Haloperidol: Rilpivirine increases haloperidol toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 34. Rilpivirine and Hydroxychloroquine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 35. Rilpivirine and Hydroxyzine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 36. Rilpivirine and Ibuprofen/Famotidine: Famotidine increases gastric pH, reducing rilpivirine levels. Administer famotidine at least 12 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. Monitor closely for treatment failure. 37. Rilpivirine and Ibutinide: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 38. Rilpivirine and Iloperidone: Rilpivirine increases iloperidone toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 39. Rilpivirine and Indapamide: Rilpivirine increases indapamide toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 40. Rilpivirine and Indinavir: Indinavir increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 41. Rilpivirine and Isoflurane: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 42. Rilpivirine and Isoniazid: Isoniazid increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 43. Rilpivirine and Isradipine: Rilpivirine increases isradipine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 44. Rilpivirine and Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. No dose adjustment is required, but monitor closely for QTc prolongation and fungal infections. 45. Rilpivirine and Ketoconazole: Ketoconazole increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. No dose adjustment is required, but monitor closely for fungal infections. 46. Rilpivirine and Lansoprazole: Lansoprazole decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This combination is contraindicated. 47. Rilpivirine and Lapatinib: Rilpivirine increases lapatinib toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 48. Rilpivirine and Lefamulin: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 49. Rilpivirine and Levofloxacin: Rilpivirine increases levofloxacin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 50. Rilpivirine and Levoketoconazole: Levoketoconazole increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. No dose adjustment is required, but monitor closely for fungal infections. 51. Rilpivirine and Lithium: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 52. Rilpivirine and Lopinavir: Lopinavir increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Rilpivirine increases lopinavir toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 53. Rilpivirine and Lovotibeglogene Autotemcel: Discontinue antiretroviral therapy at least one month before stem cell mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Some long-acting antiretrovirals may require a longer discontinuation period. 54. Rilpivirine and Lumefantrine: Rilpivirine increases lumefantrine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 55. Rilpivirine and Macimorelin: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Allow sufficient washout time for QT-prolonging drugs before administering macimorelin. 56. Rilpivirine and Magnesium (Chloride, Gluconate, Oxide): Magnesium-containing antacids increase gastric pH, reducing rilpivirine levels. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. Monitor closely for treatment failure.
